theater: 幼發拉底河中上游與舒巴爾圖姆

battle.name: 漢摩拉比在北方的征戰
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中上游與舒巴爾圖姆
battle.brief: 前1760年前後，漢摩拉比率巴比倫軍北上幼發拉底河中游，擊破由馬里、埃什努納、舒巴爾圖姆與古提烏姆組成的北方聯軍，並攻陷馬里。卡面的埃及長矛雖出自尼羅河谷，卻與本役步兵所用者同屬青銅時代的冷兵器：綁紮銅矛頭的木桿長矛既是兩河縱隊近身戰的依托，也是攻城前結盾列陣、封堵缺口的裝備。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是前1760年前後美索不達米亞北部的聯軍對抗，交戰雙方並非對等的國家，而是聯盟對王國。北方聯軍以馬里（Mari，今敘利亞泰勒哈里里）為主體：中幼發拉底河最大的城邦，由商人王雅卡布（Yakkab）統治，國力靠商路、銅料與人口買賣支撐，軍隊以步兵、弓手與輕型雙輪戰車為骨幹，另有沿河船隊。埃什努納（Eshnunna，今 Tell Asmar）控制迪亞拉河谷，曾在南方戰線上被漢摩拉比重創，此時與馬里結盟。舒巴爾圖姆（Shubartum，即 Subartu，以亞述城為中心）、土魯克庫姆（Turukkum，即 Kutu）與古提烏姆（Gutium）一方的高地勢力亦加入聯盟；北方諸城彼此以宗屬關係、盟誓與商路維繫，並無統一指揮系統，戰時才以信使與會盟拼湊成軍——聯軍的弱點正正在此。巴比倫一方是漢摩拉比的王國：以巴比倫城為基地，握有神廟體系、書吏官僚與宮廷常備兵，能集中指揮、連續作戰多年。聯軍以國土縱深與兵力取勝，巴比倫以組織與指揮取勝，這是理解本役的骨幹。
countriesEn: This campaign of around 1760 BCE was fought in northern Mesopotamia, and the two sides were not equal states but a coalition against a single kingdom. The northern coalition was built around Mari (modern Tell Hariri in Syria), the largest city-state of the middle Euphrates, ruled by the merchant-king Yakkab. Its strength rested on trade routes, copper and the traffic in people; its army was made up of infantry, archers and light two-wheeled chariots, supported by a river fleet. Eshnunna (modern Tell Asmar) controlled the Diyala valley, had already been badly mauled by Hammurabi on the southern front, and now allied itself with Mari. Shubartum (Subartu, centred on the city of Assur), Turukkum (Kutu) and the highland peoples of Gutium joined the alliance as well. These northern cities were bound to one another by vassalage, sworn oaths and caravan roads rather than by a common command system, and an army had to be improvised at the last minute through messengers and assemblies; that was the coalition's fatal weakness. On the other side stood the kingdom of Hammurabi: based at Babylon, it held the temple establishment, the scribal bureaucracy and a palace standing army, and it could concentrate command and fight campaign after campaign. The coalition relied on depth of territory and numbers; Babylon relied on organisation and command. That is the key to reading the campaign.
people: 核心人物只有兩位。漢摩拉比，辛-穆巴利特之子，約前1792年即位，統治巴比倫四十三年，前1750年病逝；在位期間打敗埃什努納、拉爾薩與埃蘭，最後十年把戰線推向北部幼發拉底河與卡布爾河谷，是兩河史上第一位把美索不達米亞南北合於一體的君主。他留下的書信逾兩百封，語氣自負而細緻，連對被俘的敵國君主也寫信陳述自己的正當性，在當時的王室文書中相當罕見。北方聯軍的核心是馬里王雅卡布（Yakkab，又作 Yag'ab）：他是同期兩河留下書信最多的外國君主，與漢摩拉比通訊往來、交易互利，後來在埃什努納窖藏出土的一封信中則被認為曾勸北方盟主出兵牽制巴比倫——此信的作者各家解讀不一，亦有學者判為漢摩拉比寫給埃什努納的盟書。一般認為漢摩拉比之母出自馬里王室，巴比倫與馬里原是姻親之國兼盟友，後成生死對頭，這層關係令戰爭格外殘酷。埃什努納方面的君主辛-伊德南（Sin-iddinam）早前已被巴比倫打敗並被俘，漢摩拉比曾致信向他誇耀戰功；舒巴爾圖姆與胡里安山區的部族首領多不留名，只以王號或城邦名見於記載，亞述城的神廟權力在聯盟的凝聚與瓦解中扮演了看不見的角色。
peopleEn: Two figures dominate. Hammurabi, son of Sin-Muballit, took the throne around 1792 BCE, ruled Babylon for forty-three years and died of illness in 1750 BCE. In the course of his reign he defeated Eshnunna, Larsa and Elam, and in the last ten years pushed the front up the middle Euphrates and the Khabur valley, becoming the first ruler to unite southern and northern Mesopotamia under one crown. More than two hundred of his own letters survive, self-confident and meticulous; he even wrote to a captured enemy king to justify his own conduct, which is unusual in the royal correspondence of the age. The pivot of the northern coalition was Yakkab, king of Mari (Yakkab, also written Yag'ab), the foreign ruler with the largest surviving body of letters in contemporary Mesopotamia, in communication and profitable commerce with Hammurabi. A letter recovered in the Eshnunna hoard is generally taken to be his appeal to a northern ally to strike at Babylon's flank, though the authorship is disputed and some scholars read it as Hammurabi's own alliance letter to Eshnunna. Hammurabi's mother is generally thought to have come from the Mari royal house, so Babylonia and Mari began as in-laws and allies before becoming enemies to the death, and that history sharpened the ferocity of the war. Sin-iddinam of Eshnunna had already been beaten and captured by Babylon, and Hammurabi wrote to him to boast of his deeds; the rulers of Shubartum and of the Hurrian highlands rarely appear by name, only as royal titles or city names, and the temple authority of Assur played an invisible role in both the assembly and the dissolution of the coalition.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及長矛是本役最不起眼、卻最耐用的那一件。早王朝時期的埃及人把銅或青銅矛頭以繩箍綁在木桿上，桿長多在兩米上下，直身無血槽；卡面這一型出自尼羅河谷，與本役相隔一千四百餘年，但它代表的正是兩河流域步兵所用的同一類工藝——本役兩軍的長矛，都是銅或青銅矛頭固定於木桿之上，形製相近而桿長與握法各異。除長矛外，交戰雙方通用的還有複合反曲弓與銅或錫銅箭頭、斧形銅斧、石鎚、投石索、削尖木棒；防護為包皮的柳條圓盾與毛氈或皮甲。車兵使用輕型雙輪戰車，多由馬拉或亞述來的能匠製造，數量有限，用於衝鋒、偵察與追擊，並非作戰主力。攻城裝備包括高厚的土坯城牆、封閉的城門、壕溝、撞木與可移動的木製攻城塔，以及就地上壘的攻城斜坡；幼發拉底河與卡布爾河的水路同時是運輸線，軍糧、木料與攻城器材多靠船運與車載北運。卡面長矛在本役的位置因此很清楚：它不是奇兵，而是列陣與攻城的骨幹。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is the least spectacular and the most durable weapon in the campaign. Early Dynastic Egypt lashed a copper or bronze head to a wooden shaft with fibre bindings; the shaft was generally around two metres, straight and without a blood groove. The card's example comes from the Nile valley and stands more than fourteen centuries away from this campaign, yet it stands for exactly the same craft the two riverbanks used here: the spears of both armies in this war were copper or bronze heads fixed to wooden shafts, similar in form but differing in length and grip. Alongside the spear, both sides used composite recurved bows with copper or tin-bronze arrowheads, axe-shaped copper axes, stone maces, slings and sharpened wooden clubs; protection was limited to hide-covered wicker round shields and fleece or leather armour. Chariot troops used light two-wheeled vehicles, mostly built by skilled craftsmen from Mari or Assur, and in small numbers; they served for shock, reconnaissance and pursuit rather than as the main effort. Siege equipment included tall mud-brick walls, closed gates, ditches, battering rams, movable wooden siege towers and ramps thrown up on the spot; the Euphrates and the Khabur served as transport lines, and grain, timber and siege materiel moved north largely by boat and by wagon. The position of the card's spear in this campaign is therefore plain: it was no exotic arm but the backbone of the line of battle and of the siege.
tactics: 漢摩拉比在北方的戰術可以分成三層。第一層是外交與神意：出師之前他要卜問沙瑪什與馬爾杜克，軍前向士兵宣示此師無故而動，是神已答應；與盟邦的誓約不必兩王見面，只需在神像前宣讀誓詞並行儀式。第二層是兵站與補給：巴比倫的軍隊不遠離幼發拉底河主軸北上，糧食隨軍並由船隻沿河接運，前哨與渡口先行控制，盡量避免在缺水缺糧的開闊地與北方聯軍主力硬碰。北方聯軍人多而各自為政：馬里與埃什努納的步兵、弓手與車兵從不同方向集結，舒巴爾圖姆與山區部隊自東北壓下，聯軍即使在紙面上兵力占優，戰線一拉長、命令一分歧，協調便告瓦解。第三層是接戰與攻城：接戰時弓手先以拋物線射擊覆蓋陣前，矛兵結盾列居中與後排，車兵自側翼衝擊缺口；對城則以圍城與切斷糧道為先，攻城塔與撞木徐徐施壓，破了城門才驅兵入城。漢摩拉比在北方遠征中也吃過敗：較早圍攻馬利吉烏姆（Malgium）時軍中流行疫病，他不得不解圍退兵，說明這支北方遠征軍並非無懈可擊。
tacticsEn: Hammurabi's northern campaigning can be read at three levels. The first is diplomacy and divine sanction: before he marched he had the omens taken for Shamash and Marduk, and he told the troops in front of the army that no one had called up this host for nothing, because the gods had already answered. Oaths with allies did not require the two kings to meet in person; the text could be recited before the divine image and the ritual performed. The second level is the line of march and supply. The army did not stray far from the axis of the Euphrates as it moved north; food went forward with the troops and was relayed by river craft, outposts and crossings were seized first, and the king avoided committing his force to a general engagement in open, waterless country against the full weight of the northern coalition. The coalition had more men but no single will: infantry, archers and chariot troops gathered from Mari and Eshnunna from different axes while the Shubartum and highland contingents pressed down from the north-east, and although the coalition outnumbered him on paper, once the line was stretched and the orders multiplied, coordination dissolved. The third level is contact and siege. On contact, archers opened with curved fire over the front, spear infantry closed behind their shields in the centre and rear, and chariots struck the flanks and the gaps. Against towns he preferred blockade and the cutting of supplies first, bringing up towers and rams by slow degrees and only storming once a gate was broken. The northern expedition was not flawless either: during an earlier siege of Malgium disease ran through his camp, and he had to lift the siege and withdraw, a reminder that this army of the north could fail.
data: 可核的數字大致如下。漢摩拉比在位四十三年，通行中年代把其統治定於約前1792至前1750年，修訂版則為前1784至前1742年，各家年代體系最遠可差近兩百年，因此本役的年序只能給出概數：戰爭落在其統治的最後數年，約當在位第三十二至三十三年。漢摩拉比的諸王年名中，有一年記作「擊敗舒巴爾圖姆、土魯克庫姆與古提烏姆之軍」，通常即指本役；法典序言的頌辭把「平定埃什努納與舒巴爾圖姆」「掃清馬里」「保全馬利吉烏姆之民」列為王權合法性的來源。馬里書信的傳世數量以千計，漢摩拉比本人留下的信件逾兩百封，是兩河同期最密集的單一君主文書群。地理上，巴比倫至馬里直線約四百公里，順幼發拉底河行程超過五百公里；考古測量常引用馬里城牆高約四至五米、牆基厚可達二十餘米、周長約九至十公里的數字。兵員、陣亡與攻城耗時在同期文獻中完全沒有留下可靠記載，本節不列臆測數字；戰爭的月份亦無依據，戰爭列表一類的編年只給年份，此處按兩河春初作戰季節取三月。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly as follows. Hammurabi reigned for forty-three years; the middle chronology puts his rule at about 1792-1750 BCE and the revised chronology at about 1784-1742 BCE, and the several chronological schemes differ by nearly two centuries, so the order of events in this campaign can only be given approximately: it falls in the last years of his reign, roughly his thirty-second and thirty-third regnal years. Among Hammurabi's year names is one recording the defeat of the army of Shubartum, Turukkum and Gutium, which is usually taken to refer to this campaign; the celebratory titles in the prologue of the Code set the pacification of Eshnunna and Shubartum, the clearing out of Mari and the sparing of the people of Malgium among the sources of the king's legitimacy. The Mari correspondence runs to thousands of tablets, and more than two hundred letters from Hammurabi's own hand survive, the densest body of documents from a single contemporary ruler. Geographically, Babylon and Mari are about four hundred kilometres apart in a straight line and more than five hundred by the Euphrates; excavation figures commonly quoted for Mari's enclosure wall put it at some four to five metres high, with a base thickness of over twenty metres and a circuit of roughly nine to ten kilometres. Troop numbers, casualties and the length of the sieges leave no reliable trace whatever in the contemporary sources, and no speculative figures are offered here. The month of the campaign is equally unattested; the chronologies of war lists give only a year, and the month of March is used here on the strength of the Mesopotamian campaigning season in early spring.
cause: 打起來是多層積累的結果。第一層是地緣：巴比倫在漢摩拉比手中先滅埃什努納、掃平拉爾薩、擊退埃蘭，兩河平原與南部已無對手，北方剩下的馬里、舒巴爾圖姆與其盟友便首當其衝，聯盟的目的很單純——不能讓巴比倫再往北。第二層是商路與資源：中幼發拉底河上游與卡布爾河谷控制著木材、銀、銅與通往敘利亞海岸的商道，馬里靠這些生意立國，巴比倫要成為兩河的主人就不能容許另一個勢力卡在河上游。第三層是同盟的反噬：巴比倫與馬里原是姻親與盟國，但各自都想成為平原唯一的霸主，盟約隨著實力變化而失效。第四層是雙方的體質：北方聯軍由數個各自獨立的城邦臨時拼湊，命令分歧、補給各自為政；巴比倫則有集中的王權、書吏官僚與神殿體系能長期支撐遠征。第五層是時機：巴比倫在南方剛打完硬仗，埃蘭的殘餘勢力尚在，聯軍把主力北調，等於把兩河平原拱手讓出——這正是漢摩拉比所等待的窗口。
causeEn: The war came out of several layers of accumulation. The first is geography: with Eshnunna destroyed, Larsa swept away and Elam driven back, Babylonia under Hammurabi had no rival left in the plain or in the south, and the remaining powers of the north - Mari, Shubartum and its allies - stood in the way; the purpose of the coalition was simple, to stop Babylon advancing further north. The second layer is trade and resources. The upper Euphrates and the Khabur valley control timber, silver, copper and the caravan roads to the Syrian coast; Mari was built on that commerce, and Babylon could not be the master of the two rivers while another power sat on the upper river. The third layer is the souring of an old alliance: Babylonia and Mari had been in-laws and allies, but each wanted to be the sole lord of the plain, and the treaty did not survive the change in the balance of power. The fourth is the constitution of the two sides. The northern coalition was thrown together from independent city-states whose orders diverged and whose supplies were their own concern; Babylon, by contrast, had a centralised kingship, a scribal bureaucracy and a temple establishment able to sustain a distant campaign year after year. The fifth is timing. Babylon had just fought a hard war in the south while Elamite strength still survived; the coalition drew its main force northward and thereby handed the plain back to Hammurabi, which was precisely the opening he was waiting for.
impact: 後果至少有四層。第一層在版圖：巴比倫第一次把美索不達米亞南北合於一體，疆域由波斯灣沿岸直抵卡布爾河谷與幼發拉底河上游，兩河不再有第二個可以與之抗衡的城邦國家。第二層在北方：馬里城被徹底拆毀，此後再未恢復舊日規模，考古層次清楚顯示這座城在舊巴比倫時代之後便趨於廢棄；舒巴爾圖姆與亞述城一帶在隨後數百年陷入衰落，直到中巴比倫時期才重新崛起，並在公元前二千紀末支配兩河——北方先由巴比倫統一、再由亞述接替，這條線正是本役之後展開的。第三層在制度：漢摩拉比把北方戰功寫進法典序言，以神授王權的正當性為統一提供解釋，刻於玄武岩石柱的《漢摩拉比法典》因此不只是法律文本，而是兩河第一次統一的政治宣言，其法理傳統後來被亞述、赫梯等國吸收改寫。第四層在史料與行政：馬里文書的毀滅是兩河研究不可補的損失，但巴比倫的書吏傳統——阿卡德語書寫、標準化文書格式與行政表格——因統一而得以推廣，成為後來亞述王國的行政骨架。
impactEn: The consequences run on at least four levels. The first is territorial: for the first time Babylonia held southern and northern Mesopotamia as one, its frontier running from the Gulf coast up to the Khabur valley and the upper Euphrates, and no second city-state remained to match it. The second is the north. Mari was torn down and never recovered its former size, and the archaeological sequence shows the city falling out of use after the Old Babylonian period; Shubartum and the region of Assur declined for the centuries that followed, recovering only in the Middle Babylonian period and rising to dominate the rivers in the late second millennium, so that the north was first unified by Babylon and later taken over by Assyria along the line this campaign opened. The third is institutional. Hammurabi wrote his northern victories into the prologue of his Code, supplying divine warrant for the unity, and the basalt stele carrying the laws became more than a legal text: it was the political proclamation of the first unification of the two rivers, and its legal tradition was later absorbed and rewritten by Assyria and Hatti. The fourth is the record and the administration. The destruction of the Mari archive is an irreplaceable loss for Mesopotamian studies, but the scribal tradition of Babylon - Akkadian writing, standardised formats and administrative tables - was spread by the unification and became the administrative skeleton of the later Assyrian kingdom.
result: 結局是巴比倫勝出。北方聯軍在接戰中瓦解，舒巴爾圖姆、土魯克庫姆與古提烏姆一方被逐一擊破，北方諸城有的歸順、有的被毀；最關鍵的一著是馬里的陷落——這座中幼發拉底河最大的城被攻破後遭到拆毀，王室被帶離，城市的商路與圖書窖藏隨之散失，馬里王國就此從兩河地圖上消失。埃什努納與舒巴爾圖姆一線隨後納入巴比倫的統治，幼發拉底河中游與卡布爾河谷自此歸於巴比倫的稅冊與徵役系統。戰役之後三年，漢摩拉比回師南下，於約前1759年徹底擊敗埃蘭，兩河最後一個對手消失；前1750年他病逝於巴比倫，繼位者薩姆蘇伊盧納接手的是前1750年由他刻下的那根玄武岩石柱。需要說明的是：具體的決戰日期、雙方兵員、攻城日程與陣亡數目，在兩河同期文獻中一概沒有留下；能確定的，是本役結束了北方獨立的城邦格局，把巴比倫的邊界推到了胡里安山區的門戶之前。
resultEn: The outcome was a Babylonian victory. The northern coalition fell apart in contact; Shubartum, Turukkum and Gutium were broken one after another, and the northern cities were either submitted or destroyed. The decisive stroke was the fall of Mari: the greatest city of the middle Euphrates was stormed and then torn down, its royal family carried off, its caravan roads and its library dispersed, and the kingdom of Mari disappeared from the map of the two rivers. Eshnunna and the Shubartum line were then drawn into Babylonian administration, and the middle Euphrates and the Khabur valley passed into Babylon's taxation and corvee registers. Three years after the campaign Hammurabi turned south, crushed Elam for good around 1759 BCE, and the last rival of the two rivers disappeared. He died at Babylon in 1750 BCE, and his successor Samsu-iluna inherited the basalt stele he had set up. It should be said plainly: the exact date of the decisive engagement, the troop strengths, the timetable of the siege and the casualty figures are simply not preserved in any contemporary source. What is certain is that this campaign ended the independent city-state order of the north and pushed Babylon's frontier up to the gateways of the Hurrian highlands.
